correctness.rationale: Exact binomial-moment identity for arbitrary integer n is established by a pathwise representation. Strict monotonicity of u(1-exp(-c/u)) proves the unique minimax crossing; exact diagonal generator-deviation calculation proves the opposite variance-proxy optimum. The small-step crossing is inverted via a strictly increasing continuous G with range (0,2a); the binomial Poisson limit, bounded moment convergence, and a nondegenerate limiting fast coordinate imply strictly positive MSE for T>0. Fixed-prob consistency and the large-step expansion are proved separately. The original seven-file package includes a standalone standard-library verifier passing 819 finite checks; finite checks are not used as proofs of quantified identities.

value.rationale: This exact natural two-mode stochastic-time-splitting model exhibits a structural conflict between variance-control design and energy-decay design and a meaningful failure of time-discretization consistency. The explicit p_h~kappa h Poisson obstruction explains why optimizing a sharp, natural finite-horizon stability measure can conceal a nonvanishing approximation error, even while reproducing the exact worst-case semigroup energy rate; this distinction is important for assessing randomized integrators. No generalization to noncommuting systems is asserted.
